claim: GENIUS (Zheng et al. 2023) explicitly reports that later iterations of GPT-4-guided iterative NAS underperform earlier iterations on NAS-Bench-201, and flags the cause as unexplained.
stance_target: prior published partial acknowledgment that LLM-guided NAS feedback loops do not monotonically improve, bearing on novelty of the target paper's degradation claim
scope_conditions: GPT-4 (full-size, closed API) on NAS-Bench-201 cell search space (15,625 architectures), CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet16-120, temperature=0, 10 iterations, 5 trials
quoted_support: "On the NAS-Bench-201 benchmark... we find that later iterations under-perform earlier iterations in some cases, and it is unclear why this should be the case given that: (i) our prompt requests improved performance, (ii) our experimental evidence suggests that GPT-4 is capable of providing improved performance. We believe future work on this problem is particularly valuable."

claim: GENIUS's raw per-iteration numerical results on NAS-Bench-201 show genuinely non-monotonic and in some trials sharply declining accuracy trajectories over iterations, but other trials show improvement, making the underlying evidence mixed rather than a uniform degradation finding.
stance_target: bounds the degree to which GENIUS anticipates the target paper's monotonic-degradation claim
quoted_support: Table 11 (CIFAR10) Trial 3: accuracy 91.28 at T=0 falls to 86.41 at T=5 and 86.33 at T=9; Table 12 (CIFAR100) Trial 4: 70.62 at T=0 drops to 65.53 at T=1 before partial recovery.

claim: GENIUS uses a random-sampling baseline methodology that correctly estimates expected-best-of-k under a fixed budget: 10 samples per trial repeated 10,000 times, averaging the best outcome across repetitions.
stance_target: methodological benchmark for what NAS reviewers expect of a random-search baseline (Q3)
scope_conditions: NAS-Bench-Macro (6561 architectures) and Channel-Bench-Macro (16,384 architectures), CIFAR-10
quoted_support: "we will perform 10 sampling iterations and subsequently identify the most optimal architectures to serve as our baselines. Nevertheless, we observed considerable variance across individual trials resulting from this sampling approach. To address this, we repeated the 10-iteration process 10,000 times and calculated the average of the best outcomes."

claim: GENIUS's feedback prompt is a single-context sequential loop structurally identical to what the target paper likely tests: the model is told the prior architecture's measured accuracy and asked to propose an improved one within the same conversation/session.
stance_target: establishes structural equivalence between GENIUS's iteration mechanism and the target paper's feedback loop, relevant to novelty/priority analysis
quoted_support: "By using this model, we achieved an accuracy of {Accuracy}%. Please recommend a new model that outperforms prior architectures based on the abovementioned experiments. Also, Please provide a rationale explaining why the suggested model surpasses all previous architectures."

claim: GENIUS reports that GPT-4 exhibits response randomness even at temperature=0, the opposite failure mode from single-template mode collapse.
stance_target: rival explanation that decoding temperature alone explains a small model's collapse to a single template (Q2 mechanism literature)
scope_conditions: GPT-4 via OpenAI API, NAS-Bench-Macro, temperature=0
quoted_support: "We observe that GENIUS exhibits some randomness in its responses, even when the temperature is set to 0. Nonetheless, despite this randomness, satisfactory results are achieved in the majority of cases."

claim: GENIUS cites EvoPrompting (Chen, Dohan, So, arXiv:2302.14838) as prior work applying evolutionary prompt engineering with soft prompt tuning to LLM-guided NAS, establishing EvoPrompting predates GENIUS by roughly two months (submitted Feb 2023 vs. GENIUS Apr 2023).
stance_target: priority chronology among LLM-NAS methods for Q1
quoted_support: "More recent work has employed evolutionary prompt engineering with soft prompt tuning to use language models for evolutionary NAS [8]." (Reference [8]: Chen, A., Dohan, D.M., So, D.R.: Evoprompting: Language models for code-level neural architecture search. arXiv preprint arXiv:2302.14838 (2023))

claim: GENIUS does not report any explicit ablation comparing feedback-enabled iteration against a no-feedback/zero-shot-only control; the only reported ablations vary training epochs and input resolution during the search stage, not presence or absence of feedback.
stance_target: gap in the literature that the target paper could fill — no prior work isolates feedback as the causal variable via controlled ablation
quoted_support: Table 3 varies "Training epochs for search stage" (10-50 epochs); Table 4 varies "Input size for search stage" (96-224px); no ablation table removes the feedback/iteration mechanism itself.

claim: GENIUS uses full-size GPT-4 via a closed proprietary API, not a small or quantised open-weight model, making it a strong-model comparison point against the target paper's small-quantised-model claim.
stance_target: model-scale contrast relevant to Q2 (is the effect scale-dependent?)
scope_conditions: GENIUS uses GPT-4 (OpenAI API), March 23 2023 ChatGPT version referenced for pilot prompt
quoted_support: "We began by simply prompting GPT-4 [ChatGPT Mar 23 Version]"
